conflicts.description: On 2026-04-02 the patient told a new physiotherapist they take nothing for cholesterol. The record shows atorvastatin 20mg at night from 2025-09-10, still being collected on 2026-07-22. The medication is active and was under-reported.

Amlodipine was stopped on 2025-11-17, but the patient listed it as current to a physiotherapist on 2026-04-02 and again on a cataract pre-operative form on 2026-06-15. A discontinued drug is being over-reported, including on a surgical form.
The 2026-06-15 pre-operative form listed metformin, lisinopril, amlodipine and eye drops, omitting atorvastatin and including a drug stopped seven months earlier. Neither error has been corrected.

patterns_to_raise.observation: The patient's self-reported medication list is inaccurate in both directions, consistently. Atorvastatin, taken throughout, has been omitted; amlodipine, stopped 2025-11-17, has been included twice. The same two errors appeared on 2026-04-02 and again on 2026-06-15.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: One of those occasions was a pre-operative form for a cataract procedure. The list a clinician receives verbally does not match the list in this record.

patterns_to_raise.observation: A dry night cough was first recorded on 2026-03-25, two weeks after the lisinopril dose was doubled from 10mg to 20mg on 2026-03-11, and has persisted since. The patient described the cough as intermittent for years, so this is a change in a pre-existing symptom rather than a new one.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: The patient has independently raised this question and wants to ask about it.

patterns_to_raise.observation: Glycaemic control improved steadily after the metformin increase on 2026-01-20: HbA1c 8.1 on 2026-01-07 to 7.2 on 2026-05-06, with fasting sugars falling from 138-155 in November 2025 to 115-125 by July 2026. Daily 30-minute walks resumed in April 2026.
patterns_to_raise.why_it_matters: Two changes coincided, so the improvement cannot be attributed to the dose alone.
